reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that raw numerical weather prediction (NWP) data lacks the granularity and calibration required for precise game-day forecasting. The paper introduces a post-processing pipeline that leverages supervised deep learning to refine NWP outputs into probabilistic precipitation classes. This process involves concatenating lead-time windows of NWP variables (e.g., temperature, humidity, surface pressure) into a channel-wise tensor, which is then fed into a neural network trained to predict categorical outcomes (no rain, light rain, heavy rain). The objective function minimizes expected loss over these sequences, with validation metrics such as CSI and bias guiding hyperparameter tuning. Temporal leakage is avoided by splitting simulations based on origin time rather than valid time. The resulting model is robust across lead times up to 87 hours, though performance degrades beyond 6 hours for pure DL approaches. The framework enables GSI to perform Bayesian inference on calibrated weather features, while GSE uses these to simulate real-time game-day conditions. The hybrid approach bridges physics-based modeling with data-driven calibration, offering a scalable solution for sports intelligence applications.
